I want to give everyone a message of hope today. I am 36 years old and have been in active addiction since I was 19 years old. August 28th of last year I overdosed after a seven month relapse. I had a 15 month old daughter at the time and not even she could keep me sober. My grandmother found me in bed unresponsive. I ended up on life support and the doctors told my grandmother I had too much brain damage from lack of oxygen and I wasnât going to survive and even in the small chance I did survive, I would have no quality of life. After five days on life support with no improvement, my grandmother made the decision to withdraw life support. The machines were turned off and my breathing tube taken out. But I didnât die, I started breathing and I opened my eyes. The doctors said I would be in the hospital for months learning how to walk/feed myself/tie my shoes, basically all the things you learn at two years old I would have to learn all over again. But, I was determined, and four days after I was taken off life support I walked out of the hospital. I am 10 months and 6 days sober today. In these last 10 months I have completed a 12 week intensive outpatient drug treatment program, an 8 week parenting class, I work a full time job and I even decided to go back to college full time and started in January and I am making all As. I finished my first semester with a 4.0GPA and made the Deanâs List, I have 3 weeks left in this semester (my second semester) and have all As in all 4 of my classes. Iâm also buying my first house this November and just bought my first brand new car in MY name 2 months ago. Hell I even met my musical hero, Sarah McLachlan twice since Iâve been sober, and was front row for one of those concerts. I just got back from an amazing vacation to Charleston, SC that I took my 85 year old grandmother on and she didnât have to pay a cent because itâs my turn to spoil her! And most importantly after losing temporary custody of my daughter after my overdose my daughter is finally coming home in September. I just want to show people that there is hope out there. As long as you still have a breath in your body, there is hope. Anyone who is struggling please reach out to someone, you can reach out to me anytime, I might not get right back to you but I will absolutely get back to you. Feel free to send me a friend request if youâd like. Whatever you do please donât give up. 

I truly hope that someone reads my story and decides to not give up. I would go through everything Iâve been through all over again if it saves just one life. You guys are more than welcome to share.

I totally forgot to mention this! I have also quit smoking and I have almost 4 months without cigarettes and I have also decided to go on a diet from all the weight I gained when I got sober. I have currently lost 32 pounds.
